story-details.user-story: As a memory engineer, I want normalized PostgreSQL tables for conversations, turns, costs, and personas, So that every interaction is queryable with metadata.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: Then the system stores user prompts, agent responses, timestamps (UTC), persona IDs, and cost breakdown
And indices support filtering by persona, topic, and timeframe

decision.title: UTC+0 (Lisbon) for All Timestamps
decision.impact: Store all timestamps in UTC (Lisbon timezone = UTC+0), convert only at display
decision.rationale: UTC eliminates DST bugs, database compatibility with PostgreSQL TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE

decision.title: Python 3.13 for LTS Support
decision.impact: Use Python 3.13 with modern type hints throughout
decision.implementation: from __future__ import annotations in all modules

fr.description: Define agent personas with name, system prompt, weight. Store personas in configuration (YAML + database). Support dynamic persona addition/removal via CLI/API.

pattern.name: Type Hints
pattern.description: Use from __future__ import annotations in all modules
pattern.example:
from __future__ import annotations
from datetime import datetime, timezone from sqlalchemy import Column, String, Text, Integer, Numeric, DateTime, Boolean, ForeignKey from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import UUID from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship
Base = declarative_base()
class Conversation(Base): __tablename__ = "conversations"
id = Column(UUID(as_uuid=True), primary_key=True, server_default=text("gen_random_uuid()")) user_id = Column(String(255), nullable=True) created_at = Column(DateTime(timezone=True), default=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc)) updated_at = Column(DateTime(timezone=True), default=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc), onupdate=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc))
messages = relationship("Message", back_populates="conversation", cascade="all, delete-orphan")
def __repr__(self) -> str: return f"<Conversation(id={self.id}, created_at={self.created_at})>"

pattern.name: Logging
pattern.description: Use structlog for structured JSON logging
pattern.example:
import structlog
logger = structlog.get_logger(__name__)
def create_conversation(user_id: str) -> Conversation: logger.info( "Creating conversation", user_id=user_id, timestamp=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() ) # ... implementation

pattern.name: Security
pattern.description: Use parameterized queries via SQLAlchemy ORM, never raw SQL
pattern.example:
# ✅ Good: Parameterized via ORM messages = session.query(Message).filter( Message.conversation_id == conversation_id, Message.created_at >= since_date ).all()
# ❌ Bad: Raw SQL with string interpolation # query = f"SELECT * FROM messages WHERE conversation_id = '{conversation_id}'"

test-cases.case: Test cascade deletes (delete conversation -> messages deleted)

security-considerations.item: Database credentials from environment variables only (.env file, not committed)
Use SQLAlchemy ORM for all queries (prevents SQL injection)
Validate all input data before database operations
Use connection pooling to prevent connection exhaustion
Log all database errors without exposing sensitive data

performance-considerations.item: Indices on foreign keys (conversation_id, provider_id, message_id)
Indices on timestamp columns for time-range queries
Connection pooling configured (5-10 connections, per architecture.md)
Lazy loading for relationships (avoid N+1 queries)
Use bulk inserts for batch operations (future optimization)

epic-to-story.rationale: Story 2.1 lays the foundation for Epic 2 by creating the database schema that all subsequent stories (2.2-2.5) will build upon. Document ingestion, vector search, and memory compilation all depend on this schema.
